description: JulES decomposes power-market simulation into smaller problems for market clearing and storage valuation. It uses TuLiPa building blocks and technology-specific models for assets such as reservoirs, batteries and hydrogen systems. The provider is Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate. Coverage: The ongoing NVE project targets Northern Europe with detailed hydropower and weather uncertainty. Temporal resolution is configurable, not a single fixed measured interval. Access: The public repository explains its motivation, models and dependencies. Neither model inputs nor executable code were obtained. Licence and cost: The repository explicitly identifies MIT and free redistribution under that licence. Limitations: The authors explicitly call this a prototype to test ideas. That limitation remains even though the ongoing project and associated demonstration data establish continuing development. For simulation it supports operational market and storage-planning experiments. Related resources: Related record data-nve-fram-open-power-market-dataset describes the provider’s open demonstration inputs for JulES.
